sanskrit: tato 'sya jānunā pṛṣṭham avapīḍya balād iva bāhunā parijagrāha dakṣiṇena śirodharām
english: Then pressing down on its back with his knee, he forcibly seized the demon's neck with his right arm.

sanskrit: savyena ca kaṭīdeśe gṛhya vāsasi pāṇḍavaḥ tad rakṣo dviguṇaṃ cakre nadantaṃ bhairavān ravān
english: And with his left hand grasping the demon by the waist and garment, the Pāṇḍava bent that rakshasa double, while it roared terrifying cries.

sanskrit: tato 'sya rudhiraṃ vaktrāt prādurāsīd viśāṃ pate bhajyamānasya bhīmena tasya ghorasya rakṣasaḥ
english: Then blood poured from the mouth of that fearsome demon, O lord of men, as it was broken apart by Bhīma.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tena śabdena vitrasto janas tasyātha rakṣasaḥ niṣpapāta gṛhād rājan sahaiva paricāribhiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Terrified by that sound, O king, the household of that demon rushed out of the house together with all its attendants.

sanskrit: tān bhītān vigatajñānān bhīmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ sāntvayām āsa balavān samaye ca nyaveśayat
english: The mighty Bhīma, foremost among warriors, pacified those who were frightened and bewildered, and made them agree to a covenant.

sanskrit: na hiṃsyā mānuṣā bhūyo yuṣmābhir iha karhi cit hiṃsatāṃ hi vadhaḥ śīghram evam eva bhaved iti
english: "Never again shall you harm human beings here at any time; for those who harm others shall meet swift death just like this," he declared.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā tāni rakṣāṃsi bhārata evam astv iti taṃ prāhur jagṛhuḥ samayaṃ ca tam
english: Hearing those words, O Bhārata, those demons said "So be it" to him and accepted that covenant.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhṛti rakṣāṃsi tatra saumyāni bhārata nagare pratyadṛśyanta narair nagaravāsibhiḥ
english: From that time forward, O Bhārata, only gentle demons appeared in that town, seen by the men who dwelt in the city.

sanskrit: tato bhimas tam ādāya gatāsuṃ puruṣādakam dvāradeśe vinikṣipya jagāmānupalakṣitaḥ
english: Then Bhīma, taking up that man-eating demon whose life had departed, threw it down at the city gate and departed undetected.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bhīmas taṃ hatvā gatvā brāhmaṇaveśma tat ācacakṣe yathāvṛttaṃ rājñaḥ sarvam aśeṣataḥ
english: Then that Bhīma, having slain the demon, went to that brahmin's dwelling and reported to the king everything that had happened, omitting nothing.

sanskrit: tato narā viniṣkrāntā nagarāt kālyam eva tu dadṛśur nihataṃ bhūmau rākṣasaṃ rudhirokṣitam
english: Then people came out of the city in the early morning and saw the demon lying slain on the ground, drenched in blood.

sanskrit: tam adrikūṭasadṛśaṃ vinikīrṇaṃ bhayāvaham ekacakrāṃ tato gatvā pravṛttiṃ pradaduḥ pare
english: Others went to Ekacakra and spread the news of that demon lying sprawled out, resembling a mountain peak, frightful to behold.

sanskrit: tataḥ sahasraśo rājan narā nagaravāsinaḥ tatrājagmur bakaṃ draṣṭuṃ sastrīvṛddhakumārakāḥ
english: Then thousands of people from the city, O king, came there to see Baka — men, women, elders, and children alike.

sanskrit: tatas te vismitāḥ sarve karma dṛṣṭvātimānuṣam daivatāny arcayāṃ cakruḥ sarva eva viśāṃ pate
english: Then all of them, amazed upon seeing that superhuman feat, worshipped the gods, every single one of them, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tataḥ pragaṇayām āsuḥ kasya vāro 'dya bhojane jñātvā cāgamya taṃ vipraṃ papracchuḥ sarva eva tat
english: Then they began to reckon whose turn it was that day to supply food; and learning this, all of them came to that brahmin and asked him about it.

sanskrit: evaṃ pṛṣṭas tu bahuśo rakṣamāṇaś ca pāṇḍavān uvāca nāgarān sarvān idaṃ viprarṣabhas tadā
english: Questioned thus many times, and still protecting the Pāṇḍavas, that foremost of brahmins then spoke these words to all the townspeople.

sanskrit: ājñāpitaṃ mām aśane rudantaṃ saha bandhubhiḥ dadarśa brāhmaṇaḥ kaś cin mantrasiddho mahābalaḥ
english: "As I was ordered to provide food and was weeping together with my kinsmen, a certain brahmin of great power, perfected in sacred formulas, saw me."

sanskrit: paripṛcchya sa māṃ pūrvaṃ parikleśaṃ purasya ca abravīd brāhmaṇaśreṣṭha āśvāsya prahasann iva
english: "Having first asked me about my distress and the town's affliction, that best of brahmins consoled me and, smiling slightly, said:"

sanskrit: prāpayiṣyāmy ahaṃ tasmai idam annaṃ durātmane mannimittaṃ bhayaṃ cāpi na kāryam iti vīryavān
english: "'I shall deliver this food to that evil-souled one myself; on my account there is no cause for fear,' said that heroic one."

sanskrit: sa tadannam upādāya gato bakavanaṃ prati tena nūnaṃ bhaved etat karma lokahitaṃ kṛtam
english: "He took that food and went toward the forest of Baka — by him surely this deed has been done for the welfare of the world."

sanskrit: tatas te brāhmaṇāḥ sarve kṣatriyāś ca suvismitāḥ vaiśyāḥ śūdrāś ca muditāś cakrur brahmamahaṃ tadā
english: Then all those brahmins, kshatriyas, vaishyas, and shudras, filled with great wonder and joy, celebrated a festival in honor of the brahmins.

sanskrit: tato jānapadāḥ sarve ājagmur nagaraṃ prati tad adbhutatamaṃ draṣṭuṃ pārthās tatraiva cāvasan
english: Then all the country folk came to the city to see that most wondrous event, while the sons of Pṛthā continued to dwell there.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca te tathā puruṣavyāghrā nihatya bakarākṣasam ata ūrdhvaṃ tato brahman kim akurvata pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: After those tiger-like men had slain the demon Baka, O brahmin, what did the Pāṇḍavas do from that time onward?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatraiva nyavasan rājan nihatya bakarākṣasam adhīyānāḥ paraṃ brahma brāhmaṇasya niveśane
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: They continued to dwell there, O king, after slaying the demon Baka, studying the highest sacred texts in the brahmin's abode.

sanskrit: tataḥ katipayāhasya brāhmaṇaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ pratiśrayārthaṃ tad veśma brāhmaṇasyājagāma ha
english: Then after a few days, a brahmin of sharpened vows came to that brahmin's house seeking lodging.

sanskrit: sa samyak pūjayitvā taṃ vidvān viprarṣabhas tadā dadau pratiśrayaṃ tasmai sadā sarvātithivratī
english: That learned foremost of brahmins, always devoted to the vow of hospitality to all guests, honored him properly and gave him lodging.

sanskrit: tatas te pāṇḍavāḥ sarve saha kuntyā nararṣabhāḥ upāsāṃ cakrire vipraṃ kathayānaṃ kathās tadā
english: Then all those Pāṇḍavas, bulls among men, together with Kuntī, sat in attendance upon that brahmin as he was narrating stories.

sanskrit: kathayām āsa deśān sa tīrthāni vividhāni ca rājñāṃ ca vividhāś caryāḥ purāṇi vividhāni ca
english: He spoke of various lands, various sacred pilgrimage sites, various conduct and practices of kings, and various ancient cities.

sanskrit: sa tatrākathayad vipraḥ kathānte janamejaya pāñcāleṣv adbhutākāraṃ yājñasenyāḥ svayaṃvaram
english: At the end of his narratives there, O Janamejaya, that brahmin described the wondrous swayamvara of Yājñasenī among the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnasya cotpattim utpattiṃ ca śikhaṇḍinaḥ ayonijatvaṃ kṛṣṇāyā drupadasya mahāmakhe
english: He described the birth of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the birth of Śikhaṇḍī, and the womb-less origin of Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī) at Drupada's great sacrifice.

sanskrit: tad adbhutatamaṃ śrutvā loke tasya mahātmanaḥ vistareṇaiva papracchuḥ kathāṃ tāṃ puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: Having heard that most wondrous account of that great-souled man, those bulls among men asked him to tell the story in full detail.

sanskrit: kathaṃ drupadaputrasya dhṛṣṭadyumnasya pāvakāt vedimadhyāc ca kṛṣṇāyāḥ saṃbhavaḥ katham adbhutaḥ
english: "How was the wondrous birth of Drupada's son Dhṛṣṭadyumna from fire? And how was the wondrous birth of Kṛṣṇa from the midst of the sacrificial altar?"

sanskrit: kathaṃ droṇān maheṣvāsāt sarvāṇy astrāṇy aśikṣata kathaṃ priyasakhāyau tau bhinnau kasya kṛtena ca
english: "How did Dhṛṣṭadyumna learn all weapons from the great archer Droṇa? And how were those two dear friends separated, and by whose doing?"

sanskrit: evaṃ taiś codito rājan sa vipraḥ puruṣarṣabhaiḥ kathayām āsa tat sarvaṃ draupadīsaṃbhavaṃ tadā
english: Thus prompted by those bulls among men, O king, that brahmin then narrated everything regarding the birth of Draupadī.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca gaṅgādvāraṃ prati mahān babhūvarṣir mahātapāḥ bharadvājo mahāprājñaḥ satataṃ saṃśitavrataḥ
english: The brahmin said: Near the gateway to the Gaṅgā there lived a great sage of great austerities — Bharadvaja, supremely wise and ever firm in his vows.

sanskrit: so 'bhiṣektuṃ gato gaṅgāṃ pūrvam evāgatāṃ satīm dadarśāpsarasaṃ tatra ghṛtācīm āplutām ṛṣiḥ
english: He went to bathe in the Gaṅgā, and there the sage saw the apsara Ghṛtācī, who had arrived earlier and was bathing.

sanskrit: tasyā vāyur nadītīre vasanaṃ vyaharat tadā apakṛṣṭāmbarāṃ dṛṣṭvā tām ṛṣiś cakame tataḥ
english: The wind carried away her garment on the river bank at that moment; seeing her with her clothing torn away, the sage was overcome with desire.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ saṃsaktamanasaḥ kaumārabrahmacāriṇaḥ hṛṣṭasya retaś caskanda tad ṛṣir droṇa ādadhe
english: The mind of that celibate who had practiced chastity from boyhood became attached to her; overcome with rapture, his seed fell — and the sage Droṇa held it in a vessel.

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavad droṇaḥ kumāras tasya dhīmataḥ adhyagīṣṭa sa vedāṃś ca vedāṅgāni ca sarvaśaḥ
english: From that, the boy Droṇa was born of that wise man; he studied the Vedas and all the Vedic auxiliaries in their entirety.

sanskrit: bharadvājasya tu sakhā pṛṣato nāma pārthivaḥ tasyāpi drupado nāma tadā samabhavat sutaḥ
english: Now a king named Pṛṣata was a friend of Bharadvaja; and of him too there was born a son named Drupada at that time.

sanskrit: sa nityam āśramaṃ gatvā droṇena saha pārṣataḥ cikrīḍādhyayanaṃ caiva cakāra kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ
english: That son of Pṛṣata, bull among kshatriyas, would always go to the hermitage and together with Droṇa would sport and study.

sanskrit: tatas tu pṛṣate 'tīte sa rājā drupado 'bhavat droṇo 'pi rāmaṃ śuśrāva ditsantaṃ vasu sarvaśaḥ
english: After Pṛṣata passed away, Drupada became king; and Droṇa heard that Rāma was giving away all his wealth.

sanskrit: vanaṃ tu prasthitaṃ rāmaṃ bharadvājasuto 'bravīt āgataṃ vittakāmaṃ māṃ viddhi droṇaṃ dvijarṣabha
english: To Rāma who was departing to the forest, the son of Bharadvaja said: "Know me, O best of twice-born, as Droṇa, who has come seeking wealth."

sanskrit: rāma uvāca śarīramātram evādya mayedam avaśeṣitam astrāṇi vā śarīraṃ vā brahmann anyataraṃ vṛṇu
english: Rāma said: Only my body alone remains to me now as my possession; choose either my weapons or my body, O brahmin — one or the other.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca astrāṇi caiva sarvāṇi teṣāṃ saṃhāram eva ca prayogaṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ dātum arhati me bhavān
english: Droṇa said: You should give me all weapons, together with their means of withdrawal, and the method of application of each and every one of them.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca tathety uktvā tatas tasmai pradadau bhṛgunandanaḥ pratigṛhya tato droṇaḥ kṛtakṛtyo 'bhavat tadā
english: The brahmin said: Saying "So be it," the son of Bhṛgu thereupon gave them to him; having received them, Droṇa then considered his purpose accomplished.

sanskrit: saṃprahṛṣṭamanāś cāpi rāmāt paramasaṃmatam brahmāstraṃ samanuprāpya nareṣv abhyadhiko 'bhavat
english: Overjoyed in heart, having received from Rāma the most excellent Brahmāstra, he became superior to all men.

sanskrit: tato drupadam āsādya bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān abravīt puruṣavyāghraḥ sakhāyaṃ viddhi mām iti
english: Then the powerful son of Bharadvaja, tiger among men, approached Drupada and said: "Know me as your friend."

sanskrit: drupada uvāca nāśrotriyaḥ śrotriyasya nārathī rathinaḥ sakhā nārājā pārthivasyāpi sakhipūrvaṃ kim iṣyate
english: Drupada said: A non-vedic scholar cannot be the friend of a vedic scholar; a non-chariot-warrior cannot be the friend of a chariot-warrior; nor can a non-king be the friend of a king — what does this former friendship matter?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca sa viniścitya manasā pāñcālyaṃ prati buddhimān jagāma kurumukhyānāṃ nagaraṃ nāgasāhvayam
english: The brahmin said: Having decided in his mind, that wise man set out toward Pāñcāla and went to the city of the chief Kurus, called Nagasahvaya (Hāstinapura).

sanskrit: tasmai pautrān samādāya vasūni vividhāni ca prāptāya pradadau bhīṣmaḥ śiṣyān droṇāya dhīmate
english: Bhīṣma, upon his arrival, gave the wise Droṇa his grandsons along with various riches, as pupils.

sanskrit: droṇaḥ śiṣyāṃs tataḥ sarvān idaṃ vacanam abravīt samānīya tadā vidvān drupadasyāsukhāya vai
english: Then the learned Droṇa, having assembled all his pupils, spoke these words for the purpose of bringing grief to Drupada:

sanskrit: ācāryavetanaṃ kiṃ cid dhṛdi saṃparivartate kṛtāstrais tat pradeyaṃ syāt tad ṛtaṃ vadatānaghāḥ
english: "Something in the way of a teacher's fee turns over in my heart; when you have mastered weapons, that should be given — tell me truly, O sinless ones."

sanskrit: yadā ca pāṇḍavāḥ sarve kṛtāstrāḥ kṛtaniśramāḥ tato droṇo 'bravīd bhūyo vetanārtham idaṃ vacaḥ
english: And when all the Pāṇḍavas had mastered weapons and completed their training, Droṇa spoke these words again regarding the teacher's fee:

sanskrit: pārṣato drupado nāma chatravatyāṃ nareśvaraḥ tasyāpakṛṣya tad rājyaṃ mama śīghraṃ pradīyatām
english: "Let the kingdom of Drupada, son of Pṛṣata, ruler of Chatravati, be swiftly seized and given to me."

sanskrit: tataḥ pāṇḍusutāḥ pañca nirjitya drupadaṃ yudhi droṇāya darśayām āsur baddhvā sasacivaṃ tadā
english: Then the five sons of Pāṇḍu, having defeated Drupada in battle, brought him bound together with his ministers before Droṇa.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca prārthayāmi tvayā sakhyaṃ punar eva narādhipa arājā kila no rājñaḥ sakhā bhavitum arhati
english: Droṇa said: "I desire friendship with you once again, O lord of men; for it is said that a non-king cannot deserve to be friend to a king."

sanskrit: ataḥ prayatitaṃ rājye yajñasena mayā tava rājāsi dakṣiṇe kūle bhāgīrathyāham uttare
english: "Therefore I have striven in your kingdom, O Yajñasena; you are king of the southern bank of the Bhāgīrathī, and I of the northern."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca asatkāraḥ sa sumahān muhūrtam api tasya tu na vyeti hṛdayād rājño durmanāḥ sa kṛśo 'bhavat
english: The brahmin said: That great insult never left the king's heart even for a moment; downcast in mind, he grew thin.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca amarṣī drupado rājā karmasiddhān dvijarṣabhān anvicchan paricakrāma brāhmaṇāvasathān bahūn
english: The brahmin said: King Drupada, burning with resentment, wandered through many brahmin hermitages seeking twice-born men accomplished in ritual action.

sanskrit: putrajanma parīpsan vai śokopahatacetanaḥ nāsti śreṣṭhaṃ mamāpatyam iti nityam acintayat
english: Desiring the birth of a son, his mind stricken with grief, he would always brood: "I have no excellent offspring."

sanskrit: jātān putrān sa nirvedād dhig bandhūn iti cābravīt niḥśvāsaparamaś cāsīd droṇaṃ praticikīrṣayā
english: In his despair he would curse even his born sons, saying "Shame on my kinsmen," and he was given over to sighing, desiring to requite Droṇa.

sanskrit: prabhāvaṃ vinayaṃ śikṣāṃ droṇasya caritāni ca kṣātreṇa ca balenāsya cintayan nānvapadyata pratikartuṃ nṛpaśreṣṭho yatamāno 'pi bhārata
english: Reflecting on Droṇa's might, discipline, training, and conduct, and on his own kshatriya strength, that best of kings, O Bhārata, could find no way to requite him despite his efforts.

sanskrit: abhitaḥ so 'tha kalmāṣīṃ gaṅgākūle paribhraman brāhmaṇāvasathaṃ puṇyaṃ āsasāda mahīpatiḥ
english: Wandering on the banks of the Kalmashin near the Gaṅgā, that lord of the earth came upon a holy brahmin hermitage.

sanskrit: tatra nāsnātakaḥ kaś cin na cāsīd avratī dvijaḥ tathaiva nāmahābhāgaḥ so 'paśyat saṃśitavratau
english: There was no one who had not completed his studentship, no twice-born without a vow, and likewise none without high merit; and he saw two who were firm in their vows.

sanskrit: yājopayājau brahmarṣī śāmyantau pṛṣatātmajaḥ saṃhitādhyayane yuktau gotrataś cāpi kāśyapau
english: The son of Pṛṣata saw the two brahmin-sages Yaja and Upayāja, who were at rest, engaged in the study of the sacred collection, both belonging to the Kaśyapa lineage.

sanskrit: tāraṇe yuktarūpau tau brāhmaṇāv ṛṣisattamau sa tāv āmantrayām āsa sarvakāmair atandritaḥ
english: Those two best of sages, fit brahmins for conducting a rite of passage, he addressed with all manner of desirable things, tirelessly.

sanskrit: buddhvā tayor balaṃ buddhiṃ kanīyāṃsam upahvare prapede chandayan kāmair upayājaṃ dhṛtavratam
english: Perceiving the power and intelligence of both, he took the younger aside privately and approached Upayāja, who was firm in his vows, pleasing him with gifts.

sanskrit: pādaśuśrūṣaṇe yuktaḥ priyavāk sarvakāmadaḥ arhayitvā yathānyāyam upayājam uvāca saḥ
english: Engaged in the service of his feet, speaking sweetly, giving him all his desires, he honored Upayāja duly and spoke to him:

sanskrit: yena me karmaṇā brahman putraḥ syād droṇamṛtyave upayāja kṛte tasmin gavāṃ dātāsmi te 'rbudam
english: "O brahmin, O Upayāja, by whatever rite a son might be born to me for the death of Droṇa — for that performed, I shall give you ten million cows."

sanskrit: yad vā te 'nyad dvijaśreṣṭha manasaḥ supriyaṃ bhavet sarvaṃ tat te pradātāhaṃ na hi me 'sty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: "Or whatever else, O best of twice-born, may be deeply pleasing to your mind — all of that I shall give you; there is no doubt about this."

sanskrit: ity ukto nāham ity evaṃ tam ṛṣiś pratyuvāca ha ārādhayiṣyan drupadaḥ sa taṃ paryacarat punaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the sage replied "Not I" — and Drupada, wishing to propitiate him, attended upon him again.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃvatsarasyānte drupadaṃ sa dvijottamaḥ upayājo 'bravīd rājan kāle madhurayā girā
english: Then at the end of a year, that best of twice-born, Upayāja, spoke to Drupada, O king, at the right moment in a sweet voice:

sanskrit: jyeṣṭho bhrātā mamāgṛhṇād vicaran vananirjhare aparijñātaśaucāyāṃ bhūmau nipatitaṃ phalam
english: "My elder brother, while wandering by a forest stream, picked up a fruit that had fallen to the ground whose purity was uncertain."

sanskrit: tad apaśyam ahaṃ bhrātur asāṃpratam anuvrajan vimarśaṃ saṃkarādāne nāyaṃ kuryāt kathaṃ cana
english: "I observed that improper action of my brother following him along, and I thought: he would never show discrimination in taking something impure."

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā phalasya nāpaśyad doṣā ye 'syānubandhikāḥ vivinakti na śaucaṃ yaḥ so 'nyatrāpi kathaṃ bhavet
english: "Seeing only the fruit, he did not notice the faults that attend it; one who does not discriminate purity — how could he do so in other matters?"

sanskrit: saṃhitādhyayanaṃ kurvan vasan gurukule ca yaḥ bhaikṣam ucchiṣṭam anyeṣāṃ bhuṅkte cāpi sadā sadā kīrtayan guṇam annānām aghṛṇī ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: "He who, while studying the sacred texts and dwelling in his teacher's household, always eats the leftover alms-food of others, ever and again praising the merits of food and without shame —"

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ phalārthinaṃ manye bhrātaraṃ tarkacakṣuṣā taṃ vai gacchasva nṛpate sa tvāṃ saṃyājayiṣyati
english: "I consider my brother to be one who seeks mere material fruit, by the eye of reasoning; go to him, O king — he will perform the sacrifice for you."

sanskrit: jugupsamāno nṛpatir manasedaṃ vicintayan upayājavacaḥ śrutvā nṛpatiḥ sarvadharmavit abhisaṃpūjya pūjārham ṛṣiṃ yājam uvāca ha
english: The king, though feeling a certain repugnance, reflected on this in his mind; having heard Upayāja's words, that king who knew all dharma duly honored the worthy sage Yaja and spoke to him:

sanskrit: ayutāni dadāny aṣṭau gavāṃ yājaya māṃ vibho droṇavairābhisaṃtaptaṃ tvaṃ hlādayitum arhasi
english: "I shall give eighty thousand cows — perform the sacrifice for me, O lord; you ought to gladden me who am scorched by enmity toward Droṇa."
